tagline.text: An uninhabited island with a long white-sand beach off western Coron

location.label: Location
location.text: Off western Coron, Palawan; reached by boat from Coron Town (shown on maps as part of Culion)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day to full day (hopping tour about 8 hours)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,300~2,500 (per person on a joiner tour; environmental fee may be extra)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Busuanga Airport (USU, Francisco B. Reyes Airport)

children.text: Malcapuya Island is an uninhabited island off western Coron, known for its long, soft white-sand beach and clear water. There is no scheduled boat service for individuals, so you go on an island-hopping tour from Coron Town (such as Tour C, which combines it with Banana Island and Bulog Dos), and the boat ride takes about 1.5–2 hours.

Malcapuya Island is a small island in the waters west of the Coron area in northern Palawan. Because nobody lives there, the scenery is not lodging and shops but a long stretch of white sand, blue water and rocks rising here and there. One Coron island-hopping guide compared its beach to Boracay and described it as quieter than Coron's lake attractions. On maps its administrative area is sometimes shown as the neighboring Culion, but travelers mostly get there by tour boat from Coron Town. One guide site said that at the time of writing the island ranked first among Coron attractions on Tripadvisor, but that is a rating that changes over time, so take it as a reference only.

To get to the island you must take a bangka from Coron Town (on Busuanga Island). There is no scheduled passenger boat, so a joiner hopping tour or a privately chartered bangka are almost the only options. The course usually called Tour C is an about
8 hours

day that combines Malcapuya, Banana Island and Bulog Dos Island, and many packages include hotel pickup, boat, guide, lunch and entrance fees. The boat is better leaving in the morning when the waves are low, and depending on the weather the trip from Coron Town to Malcapuya takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours

. What tours include varies by operator: one resort's hopping guide lists a picnic lunch, entrance fees, drinks, life vests, a snorkel set, beach towels and a guide among the inclusions and says an outrigger bangka carries up to 14 people. Some joiner tours, on the other hand, state that snorkeling gear is not included, so compare the inclusion and exclusion lists on the booking page carefully. Many packages can be cancelled up to a day ahead, but the conditions differ by product.

On the island you simply snorkel in the clean water or relax on the beach. One blog describes roofed beach cottages with a fan and a floor mattress, two restrooms with open-air showers, a generator used at night, and a simple stand-alone house for rent on higher ground. That description predates the early 2020s, though, so the current facilities may have changed. The reason Malcapuya is popular on Coron tours is that its beach is long for the size of the island and time seems to slow down the longer you stay. If Coron's lakes and wrecks are the adventurous part of the trip, this island is a comma in the middle of a tour where you catch your breath. Because a tour circles several islands, you do not get long on any single one, so if you like it, you can rent a private boat and spend more time on this island alone.

One important point: the same blog warns that work on a new resort has begun on the island and it is uncertain how long it will stay open to the public. The prices in this guide vary widely by operator and season, so I have mostly given ranges. Before you leave, check with your tour operator that a Malcapuya stop is confirmed and whether the entrance fee and environmental fee are included in the price.
Soft white sand stretches long enough that one guide compares it with Boracay. There are relatively few people, which also makes it good for photos.

The water is described as clear and good for swimming and snorkeling. Many tours do not include snorkeling gear, so bring your own or rent it. In shallow water, watch your footing so you do not step on coral.
Oddly shaped rocks rise here and there along the beach. Walking along the shoreline gives you views from different angles.

blocks.title: Tour C: Banana Island and Bulog Dos

children.text: The same tour also stops at two nearby islands. On Banana Island you relax on hammocks and the sandy beach, and at Bulog Dos you take photos and swim.

Tours often include a local-style seafood barbecue lunch by the sea. Inclusions differ by package, so check when you book. If you are vegetarian or have allergies, tell the operator at the booking stage.

blocks.title: How to arrive before the crowds

children.text: One blog says joiner tours of 16–22 people leave around 9 a.m. and can crowd the island, and recommends a private boat for a quieter visit. Some also rate it as less crowded than Coron's lake attractions.
The island is said to have beach cottages where you can rest in the shade. One blog gave the rate as ₱750 per person, but check the current rate locally.

items.title: Tour C full-day itinerary
items.subtitle: Malcapuya, Banana Island and Bulog Dos

children.text: Get picked up at your Coron Town accommodation and go to the pier. Listen to the safety briefing and board the bangka.
Enjoy the beach and snorkeling at the first island (Banana Island or Bulog Dos, depending on the guide).
Arrive at Malcapuya Island, walk the beach, swim or snorkel.
Eat the BBQ lunch on the beach and rest.
Take photos and swim at the remaining island, then return to Coron Town.
The order of stops changes with the operator and the weather. Some days the boat ride to Malcapuya takes more than
1 hour 30 minutes
, so leave some slack in your schedule.
Rent a private bangka and leave early to reach Malcapuya before the joiner tours.
Swim and snorkel on the quiet beach.
Move on to nearby Banana Island and Bulog Dos for hammocks and photo spots.
After lunch, return to Coron Town.
Waves can rise on the way back on some days, so discuss the afternoon plan with the captain in advance.

From March 29, 2026 turboprop flights at Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport were banned, so the direct Manila–Busuanga (USU) flight no longer exists. Philippine Airlines moved the route to Clark–Busuanga; from Manila, the usual way is to take a P2P bus to Clark Airport and fly Clark–Busuanga. Direct flights from Cebu also exist.
The flight from Clark to Busuanga Airport takes about
1 hour
. From the airport to Coron Town is about
40 minutes
by car.
Flight information changes with the season, so check before booking.

items.title: Tour boat from Coron Town to the island

children.text: Malcapuya is uninhabited, so there is no scheduled boat service. From Coron Town, use a hopping tour or a private bangka.
The sailing time varies with the waves, and one guide gives it as up to about
2 hours
. Many tour packages include hotel pickup.
The price of a private bangka varies with the number of passengers and the route. Get quotes for specific amounts from staff at the local pier or your accommodation and compare them.
You can book a joiner tour on an online booking site or at a travel agency in Coron Town. Packages of about
8 hours
that combine Malcapuya, Banana Island and Bulog Dos are common.
Many packages exclude snorkeling gear, so check whether entrance fees and the environmental fee are included.
Coron hopping is most comfortable in the dry season, when the sea is calm. In the morning the waves are relatively low and the beach is less crowded, so leaving early is best.
In the rainy season the sea gets rough, and tours may be cancelled or shortened. When you book, check the refund and rescheduling conditions for weather cancellations.

During the day, a boat that leaves early in the morning reaches the beach while it is empty, and the photos come out cleanest. In the afternoon, joiner tour boats overlap and the beach can get crowded. Remember, though, that the water color looks most vivid under the strong midday sun.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The sea is often calm, which is good for hopping.
Snorkeling visibility is good, but the sun is strong.

Malcapuya Island is uninhabited, so most people stay in Coron Town. The island is said to have cottages and a stand-alone house, but availability is uncertain, so if you plan to stay overnight, first check whether booking is possible. Local tour operators often pick up from Coron Town accommodations, so staying in town is more convenient.

There are no shops on the island. Lunch is often the BBQ included in the tour; if it is not included, bring a packed lunch and water. The seafood BBQ is grilled fresh, but if you are vegetarian or have allergies, tell the operator when you book.

The day before your visit, buy water, fruit and light snacks in Coron Town. One tour mentions a local-style seafood barbecue eaten on the beach, but even on the same route lunch differs by operator, so check when booking. The beach may not have enough bins, so carry your packaging back in your bag.
When you book a tour, check that Malcapuya is confirmed in the itinerary. It may be swapped for another island depending on the weather.
Boats that leave in the morning meet lower waves and are more comfortable.
Many tours do not include snorkeling gear, so bringing your own mask and snorkel is easier.
Check whether the environmental fee and entrance fee are included in the tour price, and keep a small amount of cash.
The restrooms are basic, so travel light and bring tissues.
Choose a sunscreen that is less harmful to coral, and protect yourself from the sun with a hat and rash guard.
A dry bag and a change of clothes make the boat ride more comfortable.
Take all your trash with you when you leave the island.
Wait in the hotel lobby about
10 minutes
before the tour starts. The pickup time is usually confirmed by a message the day before.
Keep your phone and camera in a waterproof pouch or zip bag, and bring a power bank because batteries can run low on the beach.
It has been reported that resort construction is under way on the island, so check before booking whether you can visit and what facilities there are.
In bad weather tours are cancelled or the route changes. Check for a message from the operator the day before.
Prices and inclusions differ greatly between operators.
Wear a life vest when snorkeling and avoid places with strong currents.
There are no medical facilities on the island, so bring basic medicine.
Do not touch corals or marine life.
You must get back to Coron Town before sunset, so avoid a late start and keep to the return time set by the captain.
